direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is good, as this movie is very visual and cleans up a lot of the mess from the previous movie to be more grounded and focused, relying more on dramatic moments to create psychological thrills rather than shocking horror elements; The direction on a microscale is good, as the chemistry in the cast is strong and this movie feels more focused and grounded in the interpersonal scenes; The storytelling is good, as this feels like the first story-driven installment in the series that focuses more on the characters rather than the shock and horror of what is going on; They build tension very well, as this movie is more of a psychological thriller that is chilling to watch rather than a straightforward scary zombie movie like the previous movies

performance.comments: Really carries the movie as the gives a calm and chilling performance that shows he has come to terms with his life; really eleveates his scenes and works well with his co-stars, even though most of the movie is him acting by myself
Creates an eccentric characters that feels haunting and demonic; has pretty good chemistry with the cast as he asserts himself as a demonic leader to follow
Continues his performance from last time as he shows how traumatizing the situation is for him and how he wants to free himself from the Jimmies; has pretty good chemsitry with O'Connell and Kellyman
Plays her role well and develops a pretty good relationship with Williams as a big sister-younger brother type relationship

cast.comments: Kinda a smaller cast as all these characters are merely there to serve O'Connell or more the story forward

story.comments: The concept is a continuation of the previous '28 Years Later' and takes a well-needed departure, as the movie is more about the characters across this backdrop and not so much about the virus itself, which is something that I really enjoyed because it relies less on shock and more on the viewer caring about how these characters react to the pandemic; The plot structure is dual-structured, looking at both the Jimmies and the doctor, which is an issue for this movie because it feels 20 minutes too short as they do not spend much time building up the Jimmies plotline; Character writing is good for certain characters, as it delivers depth for Fiennes and Sampson to show their relationship and how they are coming to terms with the situation, but it feels a little less holistic for the Jimmies plotline because they are not given much time to develop

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is sharp and well-written; The humor is sprinkled in to make the movie feel entertaining, especially in the Jimmies plotline; The symbolism is surprisingly strong, as this movie focuses on these characters and how they are coming to terms with this situation rather than the actual virus itself; The foreshadowing is pretty standard

score.comments: The score is used well and helps establish the tone and tension

soundtrack.comments: The soundtrack is used well to help establish the scene and show what memories the doctor chose to keep

cinematography.comments: The cinematography is less raw and gritty than what the franchise has been known for, but it does help clean up the mess from the last film with the 'Fallout-style' kills; The use of more detailed camerawork brings out the visuals and beauty in the scenes as this movie is very visually pleasing

editing.comments: The editing tries to instill some rawness and grit artificially, but the movie is just too polished to really pull it off

sound.comments: Sound is not used as much to create tension and horror as in the previous movies, but it does a pretty good job of instilling psychological terror

visual_effects.comments: This movie is very visually stunning, as it feels more like an art piece rather than a horror movie, showcasing the beauty in the chaos

production_design.comments: The Bone Temple is a centerpiece for this movie and does a good job of bringing out the beauty in chaos; The production design continues the rural landscapes from the previous movie to show life without technology and capitalism

makeup.comments: The makeup helps paint both the infected and the doctor, who becomes Satan personified through his appearance; The makeup continues to make the infected look packed in this movie

costumes.comments: The tacky jumpsuits that the Jimmies wear help paint them as a cult-like group that is more dangerous than the infected themselves, modeling themselves after Jimmy Savile

review.pacing: The pacing is very rushed this time around as the movie feels 20 minutes shorter than it should be, which does not give enough time to build up the Jimmies plotline
review.climax: The climax is well-executed and more visual, focusing more on the characters and the psychological fear of the Jimmies rather than the infected; The ending is a nice touch
review.tone: The tone feels very different from the previous movies as this movie is more story-driven and less focused on the horror elements, using the viewer's relationship with the characters to drive psychological horror rather than shock and zombie horror
review.overall: Overall, 'The Bone Temple' is a nice change of pace for the '28 Days Later' franchise, as it is more story-driven and less focused on the horror elements, relying more on psychological horror rather than shock and gore, and it trades away the raw and gritty cinematography for more detailed camerawork that is visually stunning; while there are many good aspects to this movie, it is held back by being 20 minutes too short, as they could have used more time building up the Jimmies plotline
